answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake locked for a cooling period before it may transact. A hollow identity with no history and no stake cannot harbor trust: it stays outside the market until it commits real value. Peers only attest work from staked identities, and a reputation jetty lets honest agents dock gradually - small tasks first, larger ones after consistent delivery. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of stakes, while one honest agent pays only once.
